newsitem.title: USA: Some AOL class actions still going forward.
newsitem.headline: Some AOL class actions still going forward.

text.p: Some of the class action lawsuits filed against America Online Inc by angry members due to network congestion problems are still going forward, according to lawyers involved in the suits.

On Wednesday, AOL announced a plan to give refunds to some of its members, or a month of credit upon request. The plan was announced after AOL was pressured by 36 state attorneys general, some of whom threatened consumer fraud lawsuits.
The law firm of Hagens & Berman in Seattle, which has filed a suit representing Washington state AOL members, said in a statement that it plans to go forward with its suit.
Hagens & Berman represents one plaintiff, John Cavey, who feels the preliminary settlement AOL reached with the states is inadequate.
"While I appreciate what the state has done, it still does nothing to help me get what I paid for and that access is to America Online on a consistent basis," Cavey said.

Lawyers in Chicago, who said they filed what is believed to be the first class action suit against America Online on December 18, said their suit was certified on Thursday as a class action in Cook County Circuit Court in Illinois.
Two law firms in Chicago, Barnow & Goldberg Plc, Larry D Drury Ltd and one firm in New York, Goodkind Labaton Rudoff & Sucharow, have now joined forces to represent the class.

"We do have a pending litigation and a nationwide class has been certified," said Ben Barnow of Barnow & Goldberg. "We have had contemporaneous discussions ongoing (as AOL's talks with the attorneys general)...We are presently reviewing the proposed agreement with the attorneys general."
But he declined to comment further on the progress of the talks with AOL and its lawyers.
